summary: Podcast with Mohan Nanwani (Head of Research, Dharohar Capital Partners) on his stock-picking framework: QGARP - Quality first (ROCE min 20%, management quality, earnings quality, company 10+ yrs old), then Growth (earnings/top-line, industry tailwinds), then Valuation last (PE vs banks P/B since money is the raw material); never start from low PE to avoid value traps. Sector views: avoids banking/credit entirely and avoids FMCG/IT defensives; themes he is overweight on are data centers (plays ancillaries), pharma/healthcare (best fund contributor despite US tariff noise), and power/energy; prefers ancillaries over OEMs, and says never invest in micro-caps/SMEs. India market outlook very bullish: sees 55-60%+ index-level gains over 3 years aided by FCNR bond inflows (~$80B) supporting the rupee and FIIs returning. Calls: none (educational, no explicit recommendations).
